headline: MD simulations map allosteric and DNA-processing mechanisms across three systems
label: Molecular Dynamics Sampling And Validation
summary: Microsecond MD and chain-of-replicas path optimization now tie simulated ensembles to quantitative mechanistic readouts.
synthesis: The shared thread is the use of molecular dynamics to convert sampled conformational ensembles into mechanistic readouts. Microsecond MD and residue interaction network analysis attribute the activity of two p53 Y220C stabilizers to restoration of an allosteric network. Chain-of-replicas path optimization maps ATP-driven ssDNA translocation by XPD and DinG, including intermediates and kinetics, with links to genetic disease etiology. MD simulations also predict that the platinum compound Aurkine16, which forms [Aurki-GGG]3+ complexes, causes DNA double-strand breaks. What is new is the explicit linkage of sampled ensembles or pathways to quantitative mechanistic or predictive claims. The three systems are heterogeneous, so the common element is methodological rather than a single mechanism.
